items.t: Oil sludge and oil starvation
items.job: Drop oil pan, clean sludge and oil pickup, update crankcase ventilation
items.note: If bearings are already damaged, a used or rebuilt engine usually runs several thousand dollars.

items.t: Ignition module can overheat and stall the engine (recall)
Timing chain or balance shaft chain rattle
items.job: Replace timing or balance shaft chain, guides and tensioner
items.note: Owners report about $800–$1,200; more if a broken guide damaged other parts.

items.t: Worn intake valves causing hard cold starts and misfires
items.job: Cylinder head valve job (replace intake valves)
items.note: Owners report $1,200–$4,000; a rebuilt cylinder head is an alternative.

items.t: Turbocharger oil leak or failure
items.job: Replace turbocharger and oil feed/return lines
items.note: Fixing a leaking oil line alone costs far less.

items.t: Crankcase ventilation (PCV) failure causing oil leaks and smoke
items.job: Replace PCV hoses, check valves and drain box (update kit)

items.t: Water pump leak
Coolant loss from cracked reservoir or hoses
items.job: Replace coolant expansion tank or leaking hose
items.note: A pressure test to find the leak may add an hour.

items.t: Oil leak from the oil level sensor
items.job: Reseal or replace oil level sensor

items.t: Thermostat stuck open
items.note: The 2.8 V6 costs more, about $880 or more at a shop.

items.t: Ignition coil failure causing misfire
items.note: Price depends on how many coils are replaced.

items.t: Steering column module (CIM) failure
items.job: Replace and program column integration module
items.note: Owners report about $900–$1,300 at a dealer.

items.t: Key fob or key chip failure
items.note: Some owners report bills up to about $1,200.

items.t: Power windows reopening slightly after closing
items.job: Adjust window and re-learn anti-pinch positions

items.t: Power window regulator or motor failure
A/C compressor failure
items.job: Replace A/C compressor, receiver/drier and recharge

items.t: Broken heater air-direction control shaft
Steering rack mount cracking the firewall
items.job: Repair firewall cracks and fit a steering rack brace

items.t: Fuel pump or fuel gauge sender failure
items.note: Based on owner costs for the closely related Saab 9-5 ($500–$1,200).

items.t: Accelerator pedal sensor codes and reduced power
items.job: Diagnose accelerator pedal sensor codes (pedal sensor and wiring check)
items.note: Diagnosis only: the fix depends on whether the pedal sensor or its wiring is at fault, so the shop has to test first. YourMechanic estimates $95–$115 for the check engine light inspection; a new pedal assembly or wiring repair costs extra.

items.t: Broken coil spring
items.job: Replace front coil springs (one or a pair)
items.note: Lesjofors aftermarket springs for 2004–2010 9-3s are about $82 each. ClickMechanic lists about 0–1 hour of labor per front spring. Replacing in pairs is best, and an alignment may add about $100.

items.t: Worn stabilizer bar end links
items.job: Replace both front stabilizer bar end links
items.note: 1A Auto sells front link pairs for about $35–$37; YourMechanic's average parts cost is about $99. YourMechanic estimates about $300–$450 total; RepairPal shows $699–$769 for a 2004.

items.t: Driver airbag inflator may rupture (recall)
Fuel pump may seize and stall the engine (recall)
Fuel lines at the pump can loosen and leak (recall)
Brake booster check valve can fail (recall)
Front seat belt may not retract on sedans (recall)
Convertible driver seat belt may not retract (recall)
Front seatback may fold forward in a crash (recall)
